newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Holyman sweetens preference issue terms.
newsitem.headline: Holyman sweetens preference issue terms.

text.p: Ferry operator Holyman Ltd said on Monday it would vary the terms of its A$49.1 million converting preference shares issue to include a free attaching option.
The options over ordinary shares will have an exercise price of A$2.00 and are exercisable up to August 30, 2002.
In a statement the company said the terms of the issue had been varied as a result of the fall in the price of Holyman shares since the company's profit downgrade announced on August 13.
On August 13, Holyman said it had reduced its year net profit forecast to the range of A$11.5 million to A$13.5 million from a A$14 million to A$16 million range predicted on June 6.

From A$3.10 prior to the downgrade announcement the shipping operator's shares sank 49 percent to a record low of A$1.578 in early trade this morning before finding support and bouncing 15 cents to A$1.75 by 3.35 p.m. (0535 GMT).
The preference share issue is to partly fund Holyman's acquisition of Union Shipping Group.
The converting preference shares are to be issued at A$4.50 apiece in a one for six entitlements issue to holders of ordinary shares.

The preference shares would convert into between one and 4.5 Holyman ordinary shares with conversion on or before August 31, 2001. The shares would pay fully franked dividends of eight percent of the issue price, starting on February 28, 1998 and be paid half yearly.
